subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw accept this native-runtime exception to the normal Doctor-owned migration rule and the resulting one-way SQLite cutover for macOS PortGuardian state?
rationale: The implementation intentionally changes the supported downgrade and concurrent-app-copy contract; source review can assess mechanics but cannot choose whether that product and operational tradeoff is acceptable.

options.title: Accept the bounded native cutover
options.body: Merge the prerequisite, retain signed-app proof, and accept native ownership only for the Darwin-lock and signed mixed-copy interoperability path.

options.title: Require a Doctor-owned migration
options.body: Keep the current JSON ledger path until a Doctor-based design can meet the legacy-writer coordination and recovery requirements.

options.title: Defer the cutover
options.body: Leave both migrations unmerged until maintainers decide whether mixed-version exclusion and no JSON-only downgrade are acceptable.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded native cutover
recommendation.body: Merge the prerequisite, retain signed-app proof, and accept native ownership only for the Darwin-lock and signed mixed-copy interoperability path.

likelyOwner.reason: This person owns the active linked native-state migration stack and explicitly requested maintainer approval of these contracts.
